mock_data.title: Modern Celebrities
mock_data.passage:
Television and the media are regularly blamed for what is thought to be wrong with modern society. So it comes as no surprise that they are held responsible for today's apparent obsession with celebrities.

The strange thing about many of those who are considered to be famous these days is that there is little reason or basis for their fame. Some of them may be film stars, football players or popstars. Others, though, seem to achieve fame on the grounds, for example, that they are a friend of someone famous, that they wear rather strange, flamboyant clothes, or that they behave exceptionally badly in public. Indeed it is notoriety rather than fame that some so-called celebrities achieve.

Of course, other generations have had their icons, but in the past fame seemed to be based more on talent and was longer lasting. The fame of today's celebrities is often very ephemeral indeed and they do not remain famous for long. They are in the headlines for a few weeks, and then fade from the scene. Compare this with the fame of some of the Hollywood greats, such as James Dean. Many of them remain legends long after their deaths.

The celebrities of today will do anything to go on appearing in the tabloids. Image is all-important to them and they just love publicity. Often they claim that they object to the paparazzi taking photographs, but they simply cannot live without the attentions of the media.

Once they are in the public eye, they are desperate to stay there, it seems. The worst thing that can happen to them is that attention is paid to someone else. Anything they do is subject to hype, image-makers being employed to ensure that their entire lives are conducted in a blaze of publicity.

They seek wealth as well as fame, although most of this is spent on their extravagant lifestyles. If all else fails, they give sensational interviews about being cured of alcohol addiction, drug addiction or eating disorders. It's sad but many of today's heroes are not very heroic.
mock_data.passageB1:
People often say that TV and newspapers are the reason for problems in today's world. So, it's not surprising that they also get the blame for our obsession with famous people, or celebrities.

It's strange that many people who are famous today don't seem to have a good reason to be famous. Some are actors in films, football players, or singers. But others become famous because they are friends with someone famous. Or maybe they wear very unusual clothes. Or they behave very badly in public. Sometimes, they are known for bad things they do, not for being good at something. This is called notoriety.

In the past, people had icons too. But it seems that they were famous because they were good at something. Also, their fame lasted longer. Today's celebrities are often famous for a very short time. They are in the news for a few weeks, and then people forget about them. Think about famous actors from Hollywood like James Dean. People still remember them many years after they died. They are legends.

Today's celebrities will do anything to be in the newspapers. How they look, their image, is very important to them. They love it when people write about them. Sometimes they say they don't like it when paparazzi take their photos. But they need the attention of the media.

Once they are famous, they want to stay famous. The worst thing for them is when people start paying attention to someone else. Everything they do is made to seem more important than it is. People who work for them, image-makers, make sure that everyone knows about their lives. They want to be in the public eye.

They want to be rich and famous. They spend a lot of money on their lives. If they are losing fame, they might give interviews about problems they have had, like drinking too much alcohol, taking drugs, or having problems with food. It's sad, but many of today's heroes aren't very good people. They are not heroic.
mock_data.passageB2:
The media, especially television, often gets the blame for many of society's problems. Therefore, it's not surprising that they are also accused of fueling our current obsession with celebrities.

What's quite odd is that many individuals considered famous today seem to lack a real reason for their celebrity status. Some might be actors, athletes, or singers, but others appear to gain fame simply by being associated with someone already famous, wearing outrageous outfits, or behaving badly in public. In fact, for some, it's infamy rather than true fame that they achieve.

While past generations certainly had their icons, fame back then seemed to be based more on genuine talent and tended to last longer. Today’s celebrities often experience fleeting fame; they might be in the spotlight for a short time and then quickly disappear. This is a stark contrast to the lasting legacy of Hollywood legends like James Dean, who remain famous long after they've died. Their talent transcended time.

Modern celebrities often go to great lengths to stay in the tabloids. Their image is paramount, and they crave publicity. Although they sometimes complain about the paparazzi, they seem unable to live without media attention. They appear desperate to remain in the public eye once they've achieved it. The worst thing for them is to be eclipsed by someone else.

Everything they do is exaggerated, with image consultants working hard to ensure their lives are constantly publicised. They are driven by the pursuit of wealth and fame, although much of their earnings are spent on their lavish lifestyles. It is as if they are trying to outdo each other in displays of wealth.

And if their careers begin to wane, some resort to giving sensational interviews, perhaps claiming they've overcome addictions to alcohol, drugs, or eating disorders. It's rather sad that many of today's so-called heroes are not particularly admirable; they lack the qualities we traditionally associate with heroism. They are more concerned with self-promotion than anything else.
mock_data.passageC1:
Given the propensity to indict television and the media for society's perceived ills, it hardly comes as a surprise that they are routinely held accountable for the contemporary celebrity obsession. The relentless spotlight on individuals, often devoid of discernible talent or merit, has become a defining characteristic of our age.

What is particularly perplexing is the tenuous basis upon which many achieve this elevated status. While some may indeed be accomplished film stars, athletes, or musicians, others seem to garner notoriety simply by virtue of associating with famous individuals, adopting outlandish sartorial choices, or engaging in conspicuously inappropriate public behavior. It is, arguably, infamy rather than genuine acclaim that propels these so-called celebrities into the public consciousness. This cult of celebrity seems to value attention above all else.

Of course, previous generations have also venerated icons; however, their fame typically hinged on demonstrable talent and proved more enduring. By contrast, the fame enjoyed by today's celebrities is frequently transient, a fleeting moment in the limelight before fading into obscurity. One need only consider the enduring legacy of Hollywood luminaries such as James Dean to appreciate the disparity. Their influence continues to resonate decades after their demise, a testament to the power of genuine artistry. The ephemeral nature of modern fame stands in stark contrast.

Modern celebrities, it appears, will resort to almost any measure to ensure their continued presence in the tabloid press. For them, image is paramount, and they demonstrably relish the attention, however intrusive, that the media bestows. While they may feign objection to the paparazzi's relentless pursuit, they are, in truth, addicted to the glare of publicity. This symbiotic relationship between celebrity and media fuels the cycle of sensationalism.

Once ensconced in the public eye, they seem desperate to remain there. The ultimate fear is that the spotlight will shift elsewhere. Consequently, their every action is subject to exaggerated hype, with image-makers meticulously crafting their public persona to ensure maximum exposure. Their lives become a carefully orchestrated performance, designed to maintain their position in the celebrity ecosystem.

Beyond the pursuit of fame, there is also the relentless quest for wealth, much of which is then squandered on extravagant lifestyles. When all else fails, they may resort to sensationalized accounts of overcoming addiction or battling eating disorders, further perpetuating the cycle of self-aggrandizement. It is a lamentable truth that many of today's so-called heroes are anything but paragons of virtue, their lives often a stark contrast to the ideals they are perceived to represent. The commodification of fame has led to a devaluation of true achievement.

mock_data.translation:
Televideniye va ommaviy axborot vositalari muntazam ravishda zamonaviy jamiyatda noto'g'ri deb hisoblangan narsalar uchun ayblanadilar. Shuning uchun ular bugungi kunda mashhur shaxslarga bo'lgan g'ayrioddiy ishtiyoq uchun javobgar deb hisoblanishlari ajablanarli emas.

Bugungi kunda mashhur deb hisoblangan ko'pchiligining g'alati tomoni shundaki, ularning mashhurligi uchun kam sabab yoki asos bor. Ularning ba'zilari kino yulduzlari, futbolchilar yoki pop-yulduzlar bo'lishi mumkin. Boshqalari esa, masalan, mashhur odamning do'sti ekanligi, o'ta g'alati, shov-shuvli kiyim kiyishlari yoki jamoat oldida juda yomon xulq-atvor ko'rsatishlari sababli mashhurlikka erishadilar. Haqiqatan ham, ba'zi soxta mashhurlar mashhurlikkdan ko'ra obro'sizlikka erishadilar.

Albatta, boshqa avlodlar ham o'z ikonalariga ega bo'lgan, ammo o'tmishda mashhurllik ko'proq iste'dodga asoslangan va uzoqroq davom etgan ko'rinadi. Bugungi mashhurlarning mashhurligi ko'pincha juda qisqa muddatli va ular uzoq vaqt mashhur bo'lib qolmaydilar. Ular bir necha hafta davomida bosh sarlavhalarda bo'lishadi va keyin sahnadan yo'qolib ketishadi. Buni Jeyms Din kabi ba'zi Gollivud buyuklarining mashhurligi bilan solishtiring. Ularning ko'pchiligi o'limlaridan keyin ham afsonalar bo'lib qolishadi.

Bugungi mashhurlar tabloidlarda ko'rinishda davom etish uchun hamma narsani qilishadi. Obro' ular uchun juda muhim va ular shunchaki reklamani yaxshi ko'rishadi. Ular ko'pincha paparazzilarning suratga tushirishiga e'tiroz bildirishlarini ta'kidlashadi, ammo ular shunchaki ommaviy axborot vositalarining e'tiborisiz yashay olmaydilar.

Bir marta jamoatchilik e'tiboriga tushlari bilanoq, ular o'sha yerda qolishga umidvor bo'lishadi. Ular uchun eng yomon narsa - bu e'tibor boshqa birovga qaratilishi. Ular qiladigan har qanday narsa shov-shuvga duchor bo'ladi, imidj yaratuvchilar ularning butun hayoti reklamaning chaqnashi ostida o'tishini ta'minlash uchun ishga olinadi.

Ular mashhurlikkdan tashqari boylik ham izlaydilar, garchi buning ko'p qismi ularning haddan tashqari turmush tarziga sarflanadi. Agar hamma narsa barbod bo'lsa, ular alkogol giyohvandligi, narkomaniya yoki ovqatlanish buzilishlaridan davolanish haqida shov-shuvli intervyular berishadi. Afsuski, bugungi qahramonlarning ko'pchiligi unchalik qahramonona emas.

mock_data.translationB1:
Odamlar ko'pincha televizor va gazetalarni bugungi dunyodagi muammolar sababchisi deb aytishadi. Shunday ekan, ularning mashhur insonlarga, yoki celebritylarga bo'lgan ishtiyoqimiz uchun ham aybdor ekanligi ajablanarli emas.

Bugungi kunda mashhur bo'lgan ko'plab odamlarning mashhur bo'lish uchun yaxshi sababi yo'qligi g'alati. Ba'zilari filmlarda aktyorlar, futbolchilar yoki qo'shiqchilar. Ammo boshqalari mashhur odam bilan do'st bo'lganligi uchun mashhur bo'lib qolishadi. Yoki juda g'ayrioddiy kiyim kiyishadi. Yoki omma oldida juda yomon o'zini tutishadi. Ba'zan ular yaxshi biror narsaga qobiliyatli bo'lgani uchun emas, balki qilgan yomon ishlari bilan tanilgan. Bu shuhratsizlik deb ataladi.
